data.claim: A descriptor's agent-specific Python is exactly its hook normalizer and emitter; it is bespoke iff one of them is used by no OTHER descriptor, and the shipped 24 descriptors grade bespoke as {antigravity, cline, copilot, cursor, goose, windsurf}.
data.falsifier: Two descriptors with the same fact names but different stdin paths must grade TWO distinct normalizers: grade them as SHARED (facts-only signature) and the signature is wrong.
data.mechanism: usage() counts each normalizer and emitter over the hooked descriptors; a key used by <2 descriptors is bespoke. Two descriptors with an identical field map share one normalizer; an empty map is the shared default.
data.probe: run ddflow.services.parity.reuse.measure() and print bespoke, normalizer_bespoke, emitter_bespoke, zero_python
data.probe_output: agents=24 hooked=19 zero_python=18 rate=0.75 bespoke=[antigravity,cline,copilot,cursor,goose,windsurf]; emitter-only proxy (harness_conformance.report.zero_python) = 20/24 bespoke=[antigravity,cline,copilot,cursor]
data.question: Which descriptors need per-agent Python, given only their hook normalizer ([hooks.fields]) and emitter ([hooks] emit variant), and can that measure be a first-class report with a shrink-only ratchet?

chunk_findings.detail: The ratchet does not enforce the contract this change exists for. `test_the_bespoke_set_only_shrinks` and `R.unrecorded(recorded=BASELINE)` only compare agent ids to `BASELINE`. A new descriptor whose normalizer or emitter is used by nobody else, with an empty or missing driver delta note, still passes once its id is added to `BASELINE` (and `test_unrecorded` returns `[]` for `recorded=frozenset({"novel"})` with no note at all). The module comment and the test docstring claim that case must fail until the gap is recorded with a reason.

chunk_findings.detail: `delta_note` joins `h.delta` onto `DELTA_DIR` and treats any non-empty read as a recorded gap. `Path` replaces the base when the right-hand side is absolute, and `..` is honored by `read_text`, so the check is not confined to `templates/drivers/deltas`. A bespoke harness with `delta="/etc/hostname"` (or `delta="../some-nonempty.txt"`) and `recorded={"novel"}` makes `unrecorded` return `[]` even though no driver delta note exists; the ratchet the change adds is bypassed by the path in the descriptor field, not by a note that states the gap and its reason.
